title: Safety, feasibility and efficacy of CRT-D with left bundle branch area pacing lead - SAFE DEAL trial
summary:
Background
Many people with heart failure have an electrical problem called a Left Bundle Branch Block, which may cause an asynchronous heart beat. The standard treatment (CRT) uses pacemaker leads in the right ventricle and a coronary sinus to resynchronize the heart beat.

However, a newer technique called Left Bundle Branch Area Pacing (LBBAP) is showing better results. Instead of just stimulating the heart muscle, it plugs directly into the heart's natural "wiring." This creates a more natural heartbeat and often leads to better recovery.

The Goal
While LBBAP works well, we need more data on how it performs when combined with a Defibrillator (ICD)—a device that prevents sudden cardiac arrest. This study will follow 40 patients to see how effective this combination is.

How the study works
If you participate, the process is straightforward:
Step 1 (Enrollment): We check your heart using an ECG, an ultrasound (echo), and blood tests.
Step 2 (The Procedure): The device is implanted within 48 hours.
Step 3 (Follow-up): We will monitor your progress at 3, 6, and 12 months. During these visits, we will:
Check your device data.
Take an ECG and heart ultrasound.
Perform blood tests and evaluate your physical energy levels.

Summary: We want to show that this new way of pacing the heart is a safe and better alternative for patients with heart failure who also need the protection of a defibrillator.

interventions.name:
Use of a left bundle branch area pacing (LBBAP) lead instead of a coronary sinus lead 
in CRT-D devices. Followup after Implantation, after 3, 6 and 12 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
1) Guideline based indication for cardiac resynchronization and implanted defibrillator therapy 
2) LVEF ≤35% 
3) Complete left bundle branch block QRS duration ≥130 ms 
4) NYHA II-III 
5) Age >18 
6) Written informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
1) Planned coronary revascularization or transcatheter aortic valve implantation (TAVI) 
2) Life expectancy of less than 3 years 
3) Pregnancy 
4) Patient is unable or unwilling to provide informed consent
